thread:
maria_g: Heads up — after the FP8 per-tensor calibration change on canary, we saw a ~12% p99 tail latency regression on gpt-medium at 512 tokens. Dumping profiler traces now.

perf-bot: [alert] perf-regression detected: gpt-medium FP8_canary vs baseline — p99 +12.3%, tokens/s -8%

maria_g: quick flame extract: ```hot funcs: quant_dequant_back > matmul > attention_kv_update
FP8_canary: 48% matmul hot
baseline: 34%```

akshay_p: hmm — did the kernel selector flip? our heuristics sometimes fall back to INT8 kernel when seq_len heuristics think batch shape isn't friendly. Could be wrong choice for steady-state with KV cache filling. :thinking_face:

jonah: microbench to reproduce (local):
```
$ run_perf --model gpt-medium --batch 4 --seq 512 --kernel fp8
tokens/s: 320
$ run_perf --model gpt-medium --batch 8 --seq 512 --kernel int8
tokens/s: 360
```
That smells like batching + kernel vectorization loss, not pure quant quality.

sabrina: what's the calibration set that produced these FP8 scales? If it was long-chat-heavy it can bias channel scales and produce larger quant/dequant cost. Outliers in attention heads blow up ranges.

lee: calib set was mixed dev: 70% short prompts, 30% long contexts. We clipped outliers at 99.9 percentile. But many long-context samples had sparse but huge activations in some heads. I think per-tensor vs per-channel choice matters for attention+MLP.

akshay_p: proposal: two-phase calibration — per-tensor for embeddings & norm layers (stability), per-channel for attention and MLP weights. Also add percentile clipping + hot-token masking during stats collection.

maria_g: also runtime change: make kernel selector consider kv_cache_fill_rate so we avoid flipping kernels during early warmup. Heuristic: prefer FP8 kernel only if kv_cache_fill_rate >= 0.6 or steady-state time > 100ms. That would keep stable vectorization.

jonah: +1. Add a sampling mode that seeds calibration samples from production traces (anonymized) rather than a static curated set — distribution mismatch is the common root cause.

sabrina: and add explicit outlier logging: when a channel's clip point exceeds X*sigma, log top-k tokens that caused spike. We'll then decide to exclude those tokens from calibration or handle via hotword masking.

lee: I'll open a small PR: - add kv-fill metric to selector - add two-phase calib config - add sampler toggle to pipeline. Also add a CI perf check: compare tokens/s on 3 datasets: dev-synth, prod-sampled, long-tail-chat.

maria_g: perfect. I'll attach the profiler traces + sample ids to the issue and coordinate the canary A/B: we should gate rollout until the new selector + two-phase calib passes the prod-sampled test. Tagging @eng-runtime for kernel selector review.

perf-bot: run queued: ci/perf/gpt-medium/fp8-canary (job 3287) — status: queued

akshay_p: one more thought — consider preferring INT8 kernel for short-burst traffic but FP8 for steady-state; we can make that decision via a decaying estimator of kv_fill_rate so transient traffic won't trigger kernel flips.

maria_g: agreed. We'll prototype the decaying estimator in the selector PR. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
